Algorithm 1: Reproductive Capacity Assessment Mechanism.
1: Input: Chromosome population size N, test population size S, population division ratio parameter β
2: Output: Reproductive subpopulation pop1, ordinary subpopulation pop2
3: Generate a test population of size S randomly
4: For i=1 To N
5: For j=1 to S do
6: a) Perform crossover between individual i and individual j to produce offspring
7: b) If the offspring dominates individual i, replace individual i with the offspring and increment the reproductive capability of individual i by 1
8: End
9: End
10: For i=1 To N do
11: If (reproductive capability of individual i > average reproductive capability)
12: Individual i belongs to the reproductive subpopulation pop1
13: Else
14: Individual i belongs to the ordinary subpopulation pop2
15: End for

Operator TypesOperator Designs
Classical operatorsRandomly select two operations, swap their positions. Randomly select one operation and insert it at a specified position. Randomly select two operations, insert one operation before another. Randomly select two operations, insert one operation after another.
Disruptive and reconstructive operatorsRandomly generate a binary array (0–1), retain positions with 1, randomly redistribute positions with 0. Randomly select a point, maintain positions to the right, shuffle positions to the left. Randomly select a point, maintain positions to the left, shuffle positions to the right. Randomly select two points, disrupt operations between the two points.
Critical path operatorsRandomly select an operation on the critical path, randomly move all operations of its job to another factory. Randomly select an operation on the critical path, use a roulette wheel selection method to choose a processing factory, move all operations of its job to the selected factory. Randomly select an operation on the critical path, randomly reselect a machining center within its available range. Randomly select an operation on the critical path, use a roulette wheel selection method to choose a machining center, move the current operation to the selected machine for processing.

8: reward = 0

Input: Number of iterations (G), population size (ps), scaling parameter (β), crossover probability ( \( P_{c} \) ),
1: mutation probability ( \( P_{m} \) ), batch size (batch), learning rate (α), epsilon-greedy coefficient (ε), discount factor (γ)

3: Initialize population randomly

4: Initialize D3QN network (batch, α, ε, γ)

5: For g=1 to G do

6: pop1, pop2←Reproductive capacity assessment mechanism split population

8: For i=1 to len(pop1) do

9: C1, C2←Standard evolution operators ( \( P_{c} \) ,  \( P_{m} \) )

10: pop1 ← pop1 ∪ C1 ∪ C2

11: pop1 ← Remove duplicates (pop1)

13: End

15: C1, C2←Improved evolution operators ( \( P_{c} \) ,  \( P_{m} \) )

16: pop2 ← pop2 ∪ C1 ∪ C2

17: pop2 ← Remove duplicates (pop2)

18: pop2 ← Energy-saving strategy (pop2)

21: {F0, F1, ...} ← Fast non-dominated sorting (C)

22: C' ← Crowding distance calculation{F0, F1, ...}

23: pop←C' (1:ps, :)

24: P ← Remove duplicates (PF ∪ F0)

25: P, Qθ ← Operator selection mechanism based on D3QN (P, batch, α, ε, γ)

26: g = g + 1

27: End
